description:
FOUND (s526w1, HTTP-Message t/message-decode-zipbomb.t: no TAP, "Heap exhausted during allocation").
Probe (scratch p-zb.pl): build "\0" x 16M, gzip it three times (Level 9, -Minimal) -- PCL OK but 20 s / 245 MB (perl 0.15 s / 44 MB); then gunzip three times: rounds 1-2 OK, round 3 (16 MB output) dies "Heap exhausted ... 52199440 requested" at 55 % of the 1 GB heap.
Backtrace: SB-KERNEL:VECTOR-SUBSEQ <- (LAMBDA NIL :IN PCL::%P-STRBUF-INSTALL) <- %PCL-DEFINEDP <- P-DEFINED <- IO::Uncompress's read loop.  `defined $$out` between appends installs (copies) the whole growing :str-buffer each time: quadratic copying, and two 50 MB copies alive at once.  FIX SHAPE (to measure first): `defined` (and other reads that do not need the characters: length?) answer from the buffer without materializing; or install without copying when the buffer is not shared.  Rows: message-decode-zipbomb.t 9 (a *FILE* row on the board).  Layer: cl/ runtime -- bench KIND (exclusive), full sweep.

=== QUEUED (s530, Fable, 2026-10-31) ===
One of the 41 REAL whole-file CPAN board failures (the USER-asked review; 138 FAIL files = 69 perl-skips + 4 fixed + 2 perl-fails + 22 ruled not-supported + 41 real).  Queued as s531b member 9 (HTTP-Message) -- `briefs-and-rules-for-claude-subagents/s530/s531a-prompt.md` / `s531b-prompt.md`.


=== DONE (s532d) ===
FIX (cl/ only, emission IDENTICAL): the readers that ask only WHAT a private-buffer scalar is (a :strbuf cell #2115 or a :memfh cell #2111 -- always a string) answer from the box WITHOUT the getter's whole-buffer snapshot, through ONE predicate %p-private-buffer-box-p (%p-slot-live-length now uses it too): %pcl-definedp is T; %scalar-holds-ref-p is NIL (a ref to it is SCALAR, never REF); p-scalar answers the box itself -- every `($)` prototype slot is a p-scalar, and perl's scalar() passes the SV (a dualvar box already did this); a p-defined compiler macro peeks an element (`defined $h{K}` / `defined $a[I]`) through the same %p-peek-* path p-length / p-substr / p-=~ use (#2881).  The backtraces named the three readers in turn: IO::Uncompress's read loop asks `defined $$out`, `ref $out` and `Scalar::Util::readonly(${ $_[0] })` per chunk.
MEASURED (heavy.sh s532d bench 03:11-03:1x, load 1.5-1.7; scratch/s532d/out/bench3830.log; A = tree runtime, B = base 06a4b8ba, interleaved best-of-5):
    fprint       A 0.1955  B 0.1936   -1.0 %  (within noise)
    joinarr      A 0.1099  B 0.1103   +0.4 %  (within noise)
    lcbytes      A 0.1386  B 0.1396   +0.7 %  (within noise)
    strbuf-def   A 0.0036  B 0.6167   171x faster (INFO row: 20k `$h{b} .= ...; defined $h{b}`; perl 0.0012)
    strbuf-ref   A 0.0048  B 0.6061   126x faster (INFO row: 20k `$$r .= ...; defined $$r; ref $r`; perl 0.0009)
  the 16 MB zipbomb probe (scratch/s532d/pr/zb.pl: gzip x3 then gunzip x3, perl 0.17 s / 60 MB):
    base pcl: heap exhausted in gunzip round 3, 39.4 s wall, maxrss 734 MB
    tree pcl: all 3 rounds, output identical, 1.65 - 1.81 s wall, maxrss 363 - 364 MB (two runs each; base 39.4 / 39.6 s, 734 MB)
PROBES: scratch/s532d/pr/sb2.pl (16 rows: defined / ref / readonly / scalar() of :strbuf hash-element, array-element, our, deref and :memfh scalars, a write of undef, scalar() aliasing) tree == perl except one row that the base shares (`readonly(${ \"lit" })`, unrelated); base wrong on 4 more (scalar() aliasing).  RESIDUE filed: #4323 (scalar() of an ORDINARY scalar copies where perl aliases -- pre-existing; the private-buffer box now aliases like perl).
GUARD: Pl/t/perf-levers-11.t rows 11 (mechanism: the p-defined peek, and defined / p-scalar / the REF test on a :strbuf box leave its snapshot slot NIL) and 12 (perl-probed answers), inverse-verified on 06a4b8ba.  ir-spec "in-place .=" gains one normative sentence.
ACCEPTANCE FILE: HTTP-Message message-decode-zipbomb.t is held by the HEAP, not by this mechanism: at the 1 GB default both base and tree die before row 1; at PCL_DYNAMIC_SPACE_MB=1800 BOTH pass 9/9 (31.3 s / 28.9 s, maxrss 1,298 MB each) -- SBCL characters are 4 bytes, each 16 MB string the test keeps is 64 MB.  The board's *PLAN* row is re-keyed #3830 -> #4322 (filed: a per-file heap allowance for the board is the obvious first step).
subject: PERF / HEAP: a string built by repeated appends is MATERIALIZED (vector-subseq of the whole buffer) by every `defined` read -- IO::Uncompress::Gunzip inflating a 16 MB output exhausts the 1 GB SBCL heap (HTTP-Message message-decode-zipbomb.t, perl 0.15 s / 44 MB)
